question: I have a gene expression matrix in CSV format. Generate a clustered heatmap using row-wise Z-score normalization and default hierarchical clustering. Label samples and genes clearly.

files.eval_guideline: Heatmap must show row Z-score coloring with hierarchical clustering dendrograms on both axes and labeled genes and samples; color palette and font size may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The files have the identical basename and PNG image format. The candidate is in the corresponding task output directory and clearly represents the requested clustered gene-expression heatmap.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires semantic visual features: row-wise Z-score coloring, dendrograms on both axes, and clear gene and sample labels, while allowing palette and font differences. Semantic comparison is therefore appropriate for the PNG heatmap.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show the same 100-gene by 20-sample expression matrix after row-wise Z-score normalization. They use the same blue-white-red diverging scale with approximately the same range, display hierarchical-clustering dendrograms on both axes, and preserve the same clustered gene and sample ordering. The dominant scientific pattern is identical: Samples 6, 4, 7, 3, 10, 5, 8, 2, 1, and 9 form a predominantly lower-expression cluster, while Samples 12, 15, 17, 18, 11, 13, 14, 19, 16, and 20 form a predominantly higher-expression cluster. Gene labels and sample labels are present in both. Differences are cosmetic only: the candidate is taller and more compact, uses larger heatmap cells and clearer labels, places the legend differently, and provides a more descriptive title specifying average linkage and Euclidean distance. These presentation differences do not alter the data, clustering, or scientific interpretation.
